llm.summary: This is a real website-scaffolding skill, but its generated auth, payment, session, and tenant-isolation code has serious security gaps that users should review before installing or deploying.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: generate EdgeOne full-stack sites with auth, e-commerce payments, AI chat, analytics, and admin tools. The concern is that it presents production-oriented security capabilities while several included implementations are placeholders or unsafe for high-impact auth and payment flows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are mostly scoped to scaffolding and EdgeOne deployment, and the skill says deployment should require user confirmation. However, some documentation claims JWT middleware, secure cookies, payment verification, and tenant isolation that the generated files do not consistently enforce.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden install hook, postinstall script, or automatic persistence mechanism was found. Installation/deployment uses explicit npm and edgeone commands, but those commands can deploy cloud functions and require sensitive production credentials.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested secrets such as JWT, payment, AI, and database credentials fit the website-building purpose, but the scaffold grants production-grade account, payment, admin, and tenant authority without sufficiently reliable generated security controls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The generated app persists sessions, refresh-token metadata, carts, analytics, and user/account state in KV or browser storage. It also returns tokens and stores access and refresh tokens in script-readable localStorage despite documentation emphasizing HttpOnly cookie protection.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Treat this as a Review item, not proven malware. Do not deploy the generated e-commerce, auth, admin, or multi-tenant code unchanged. Before installing for production, require fixes for password verification, token storage, payment callback verification, tenant-scoped KV keys, quota/billing atomicity, analytics opt-out, and middleware enforcement; then test those paths with real negative cases.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Analytics is purpose-aligned and documented in README/SKILL as an optional module, but the app initializes page tracking automatically and the claimed opt-out support was not evident in the inspected code, so this remains an under-disclosure/privacy note rather than a standalone malicious signal.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The auth concerns are artifact-backed: register.js has a malformed duplicate-email query, login.js includes a plaintext comparison against password_hash when env.DB is present, logout can report success without reliable server-side invalidation, and _middleware.js passes through protected routes despite comments describing JWT enforcement.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The payment package concern is artifact-backed: packages/payment/src/index.js documents verifyPayment as callback verification but returns valid:true for any parseable JSON. The separate wx-notify Cloud Function has stronger checks, but the exported helper remains dangerous if reused as documented.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The tenant and quota concerns are partly confirmed: getShardSessionKey omits the tenant from the returned KV key, the payment tenant lookup example uses a global order_tenant key, and quota/billing counters use non-atomic read-modify-write despite some comments claiming atomic behavior.
[PE3] unexpected: The credential-storage concern is confirmed: client auth code stores access and refresh tokens in localStorage and exposes the access token via getToken, which conflicts with the documented HttpOnly-cookie security posture.
